short: Farming, permanent settlement and pottery reshape human society.
full:
The Neolithic is defined less by stone than by a change in how people fed themselves. Beginning around 10,000 BCE in the Fertile Crescent, communities domesticated wheat, barley, sheep, goats, pigs and cattle, and settled beside their fields. Population densities rose by orders of magnitude.

With settlement came pottery, weaving, ground and polished stone tools, and monumental construction — Göbekli Tepe, Çatalhöyük, the megalithic tombs of Atlantic Europe, and later Stonehenge. It also brought crowd diseases, stored surplus, inherited property and visible social hierarchy. Almost everything we recognise as civilisation has roots in this period.
